html:
The Treaty of Fez, signed on 30 March 1912, made Morocco a protectorate of France. Sultan Abd al-Hafid signed it with French troops in his capital, after European powers had quarrelled over Morocco for a decade.

Germany had challenged France in the Tangier crisis of 1905 and the Agadir crisis of 1911, and was bought off with land in the Congo. Spain was given the north, including the Rif, and a southern strip (Spanish Morocco); Tangier was later made an international zone.

The first French resident-general, Hubert Lyautey, kept the sultan as a figurehead and built new European towns beside the old medinas. Resistance went on in the mountains, most of all in the Rif War, until independence under Mohammed V in 1956.
sum: The Treaty of Fez, signed on 30 March 1912, made Morocco a protectorate of France. Sultan Abd al-Hafid signed it with French troops in his capital, after European powers had quarrelled over Morocco for a decade.
